A11Y/MOTION: Reduce Motion IS respected where implemented (useMotionReduced, skeleton, empty-state, button, sumaiya-mark, the web globals.css net) but the chat's own animations are the exception - TypingDot (sumaiya-chat-screen.tsx:39-50), QuickActionsGrid (:25) and AttachmentPreviewSheet 220/160 (:44-47) never consult it (X1); 160ms, 280/55ms, 320ms and 260ms are all off-token - four ad-hoc durations in one screen (X2); the web send button swaps Send->Loader2 on one frame (cv-assistant-client.tsx:3154) where the standard requires a 220ms cross-fade (X3); web aria-live sits on the typing row (:2827) and the mic error (:3007), not on a finished assistant message, and the transcript has no role='log' (X4); no timestamps or ordering affordance anywhere, so 'when did I say that' is unanswerable in a 40-turn transcript (X5). WHAT THE USER CANNOT DO OR UNDERSTAND TODAY: 1 cannot stop her - no cancel anywhere on either app; 2 cannot keep typing while she works; 3 cannot tell whether their message was delivered (no Imetumwa/Haijatumwa); 4 cannot retry the thing that failed - the error card offers no action; 5 cannot tell what is happening beyond three dots; 6 cannot tell whether their file was read - a 13px icon colour is the whole vocabulary; 7 cannot find job targeting unless their words contain the right noun; 8 cannot tell the conversation is kept (it is, 40 turns on disk); 9 cannot trust 'Boresha na AI' which returned their own text with a 200; 10 cannot explain the failure - 'AI is not configured.' is English and is not their fault; 11 cannot see what still works when the model is unreachable, though ATS scoring, PDF export, OCR and the job feed all work without it; 12 cannot open the CV she built as THEIR CV - the editor gets a copy with no id, so saving forks a second one. WHAT WASTES DATA OR TIME: the fake 1.8s progress ramp is a data-cost multiplier - a user who does not believe the screen leaves and returns, and every return is another request on a metered line; and 'Ninasoma faili...' with a static icon over a 2-attempt, 700ms-backoff upload is a screen that has already decided to retry twice and tells the user nothing while it spends their bytes.

WHAT ACTUALLY TRANSFERS TO A CHEAP ANDROID ON EXPENSIVE DATA: TAKE - step rail from real events (4 text nodes, replaces the dots); dynamic checklist instead of a percentage (no new requests); auto-collapse to a receipt; stop in the send slot (interrupts a request, SAVES the user's bytes); progress+size per chip (local only); an honest capability tier as a status (one /api/ai/status probe); the gold band on the OUTPUT not the app. SKIP - token-level streaming UI (no streaming by design, and it is the documented screen-reader failure), a live log/raw reasoning, skeleton shimmer in the chat (the rail IS the loading state). REJECT - animated or estimated percentages ('betrayal when it jumps'), Liquid Glass/backdrop-blur (per-frame GPU for no information), count-up numbers (scores are compared, not admired), a model/effort picker in the composer (the web's Haraka/Wastani/Kina at cv-assistant-client.tsx:3080-3116 is a mechanism; sell the outcome). REDUCE - haptics to one light tap on send and on the terminal state only.
message_taxonomy: Nine kinds; every one has a job; the two dead union members are retired. T1 USER TURN (Ujumbe wako) - right aligned, #B83A12 fill, #FAF5EE text, radius 18 with bottom-right 4, max-width 86%, padding 11/14; attachments are pills inside the bubble; below the text, right aligned at 10.5px, ONE delivery word: 'Inatuma...' | 'Imetumwa' | 'Haijatumwa'; on failure the bubble is unchanged and gains a 1.5px #C13E14 outline - the user's words are never removed. T2 SUMAIYA TURN (Jibu) - left, #FFFFFF fill, 1px #E9E0D4 border, radius 18 with bottom-left 4; a run of bubbles from one reply carries ONE attribution row above the first (16dp mark + SUMAIYA at 11px 800 #756A5E), later bubbles none; text 15/22 #211A15. T3 SYSTEM NOTE (Kidokezo) - centred, no avatar, #F4EEE4 pill, 12px #756A5E, max-width 88%; carries persistence ('Mazungumzo yanabaki kwenye simu hii.'), a restored turn, 'mazungumzo yamefutwa', a queued turn and a retry receipt; it is the ONLY element allowed to be centred. T4 PROGRESS RAIL (Hatua) - a card, not a bubble: full width, #FFFFFF, 1px border, radius 20, shadow-card; attribution row + elapsed 'inaendelea - 6s', a step-truthful bar, up to four step rows, a footer with the stop control. T5 DOCUMENT CARD (Kadi ya hati) - full width with a tinted header band (KADI YA HATI left, state right) - a band no bubble has, which is what stops it reading as a rich message; thumbnail, title ('CV - Amina Juma'), a chip row (template, page count), one sentence of what she used and what she could not find ('Nilichotumia: jina, uzoefu wa mauzo, ujuzi 9, elimu. Nilichokosa: namba ya simu.'), then primary 'Fungua kwenye kihariri', secondary 'Hifadhi kwenye CV zako', and a #E4EDEA footer state line ('Imehifadhiwa kwenye CV zako' | 'Inatumika bila mtandao'). T6 SUGGESTION CHIP (Chip) - one horizontally scrollable row docked above the composer on #FFFFFF with a 1px top border; chip = #F4EEE4 fill, 1px #E9E0D4 border, 12px 700 #2C231C, a '>' in #DA4A1C as prefix, 7x12 padding, nowrap; MAXIMUM THREE, and each names an OUTCOME ('Lenga kwenye kazi', 'Kagua CV yako', 'Barua ya maombi') or is her own invitation in the first person ('Ongea nami') - never a third-party feature label. T7 ERROR ATTACHED TO A TURN (Hitilafu) - right aligned under the failed turn, max-width 92%, #FFFFFF, 1px rgba(193,62,20,.35) with a 3px #C13E14 left edge, radius 16; three parts always in this order: what happened (h4 14/800), why (13/1.5 #6B5F54, with the non-cause explicitly ruled out), what to do (buttons); never full width, never a status code. T8 UNAVAILABLE CARD (Kutokuwa na uwezo) - a first-class state, not an error page (see unavailable_state). T9 RECEIPT (Risiti) - when a multi-step turn finishes the rail collapses to one pill 'v Nilifanya hivi: hatua 3' (12.5px 600 #6B5F54 on #FFFFFF); tapping expands the finished steps read-only; it never re-animates on scroll. RETIRED: type 'recommendation' and type 'action' (chat-types.ts:5 - nothing renders them). 'skill-gap' and 'learning' keep their existing cards (skill-gap-card.tsx, learning-resources.tsx) wrapped in the document-card shell so all rich content has one visual grammar. PROGRESS RAIL DETAIL: the bar is transform: scaleX(finished/total) - two of four done is scaleX(.5) - and NEVER runs ahead of the work; on completion it turns #12433D and reaches 1; only the current step's glyph carries a bounded beat so motion is attached to the thing that is moving; step states are DONE (solid #12433D disc, #FAF5EE check, text #756A5E, past tense, with a sub-line of the actual result - 'herufi 2,340 - nikasoma "Sales Officer, CCBRT"'), CURRENT (#B83A12 disc, #FAF5EE text at 700) and PENDING (hollow #9C8D7B ring, text at 75% - and it is NAMED, because a named future step is a plan, not a silence); the rail carries STOP from the first second and stopping keeps partial work and never discards the user's words; every line is emitted by a real event, there are at most four, elapsed time is plain text and never animated, a step that has not run is never faked, and a hung step changes to a stalled line with stop still available.
animations: All values are the app's existing tokens (apps/web/lib/motion.ts, apps/native/src/components/ui/motion.tsx, docs/MOTION-STANDARD-2026-09-20.md). Nothing invents a duration; the two off-token values the audit found (280/55ms in quick-actions-grid.tsx, 160ms in attachment-preview-sheet.tsx) are replaced. Format: move - entry - exit - curve - reduced motion - why it is cheap. 1 Sumaiya bubble arrives: 300 - ease.out(0.33,1,0.68,1) - instant - opacity+translateY(12), one node. 2 Bubble run stagger: 30+min(i,3)x40 (cap 3 for chat, not 6) - reduced 0 - 3 lookups, no integrator. 3 User bubble appears: NONE - their finger produced it (standard section 4, 'taps'). 4 Document card placed: 220, scale .985->1, translateY 6->0 - exit 140 ease.in - ease.out - instant - transform only. 5 Chips dock in: 300 (stagger 30, cap 3) - exit 140 ease.in - ease.out - instant - shared-row children. 6 Progress rail enters (replacing the 3-dot bubble): 300, 12px rise - exit 140 ease.in - ease.out - instant - overlaps the outgoing bubble. 7 Rail step advances: old line 140 ease.in, new line 220 ease.out - instant - two text nodes, no container reflow. 8 Rail collapses to receipt: 220 container layout on spring.snappy{22,260,.8} - instant - the sanctioned reflow case. 9 Step-truthful bar: 220 ease.out on transform scaleX - instant - transform only, never width. 10 Current-step beat: BOUNDED 1.05s, 2 cycles - ease.inOut - static dot under reduced motion - one 8px node; it replaces an unbounded withRepeat(-1). 11 Send<->stop morph: 220 glyph cross-fade + 90 fill - ease.out / micro - instant - in place, no layout. 12 Attachment chip enters/leaves: 300 (stagger 40) - exit 140 ease.in - ease.out - instant - layout on the container only. 13 Upload progress: 90 steps on scaleX, >=5% steps - ease.out - instant - transform only. 14 Sheet present/dismiss (attach, job choice, preview): backdrop 220, panel translateY 360->0 at 220 - exit 140 ease.in - ease.out - cross-fade - already in the standard, just implement it. 15 Chosen path expands: content 220 + container layout - exit 140 - ease.out - instant - the standard's expand/collapse. 16 Error card arrives on its turn: 300 rise - exit 140 ease.in - ease.out - instant - one node. 17 Retry label<->spinner: 220 in place - ease.out - instant - the standard's button composite. 18 Rail->receipt->answer hand-off: placeholder 140 FadeOut WHILE content enters 300 - ease.in / ease.out - instant - the standard's 'loading -> content'. 19 Unavailable card arrives: 300 rise - exit 140 ease.in, self-retiring on recovery - ease.out / ease.in - instant - one node, NO pulse, NO bounce, no infinite attention. 20 Card->editor handoff: FLIP card->editor header 260 - reverse 260 - ease.emphasized(0.16,1,0.3,1) - reduced motion replaces it with a cross-fade (per Apple HIG) - one composited layer. 21 Scroll-to-bottom pill: 300 rise 12 - exit 140 ease.in - ease.out - instant - it never animates the scroll offset (standard section 4). 22 Destructive confirm (clear conversation): dialog spring.gentle{20,180,.9}, backdrop 220 - exit 140 ease.in - spring/ease.in - cross-fade - the standard's dialog composite. BANNED by this redesign, with the reason: any unbounded withRepeat(-1) in the chat or the scan path (a Level A WCAG 2.2.2 failure and a per-frame cost on a Redmi-class GPU); any bar that reports more progress than has happened; any animation on the keystroke path; any animation of a number the user is comparing; any third ad-hoc duration; and a per-row spring on more than the one sanctioned container. STANDING STANDARD SATISFIED: nothing appears suddenly (every entrance is a token duration from a settled state), everything is interruptible (stop in the rail footer from the first second, and the composer stays open), reduced motion is respected at the component level for the chat's own moves (not only globally), and every move above is transform/opacity on at most the nodes involved - no per-row spring, no width animation, no blur.
unavailable_state: It is a STATE, not an error page, and it is a first-class member of the message taxonomy (T8). DETECTION: GET /api/ai/status -> {configured, provider} (routes/ai.ts:113) on chat entry, and the turn's own outcome thereafter (source:'local' counts as unavailable-for-writing). Never a connectivity heuristic. THREE VARIANTS, all in the same card. KNOWN (the probe says so, before the user types): 'Sina uwezo wa kufikiri sasa hivi.' + 'Sikutaka ujue kwa kuandika ombi na kusubiri bure - kwa hivyo nakuambia kabla.' Offers the three things that genuinely work with no model: 'Kagua CV yako' (deterministic ATS score + keyword diff), 'Fungua kwenye kihariri', 'Soma picha ya CV yako' (tesseract OCR), then a ruled-out line: 'Kinachokosekana: kuandika na kuboresha kwa maneno.' MID-TURN (the turn fails): 'Sikuweza kufikiri ombi hili.' + 'Sababu: huduma inayoniwezesha kufikiri haipatikani sasa hivi. Si mtandao wako, na si maandishi yako - ombi lako lilifika, jibu langu halikutoka.' Offers 'Jaribu ombi hili tena' (resends THE SAME turn, per QCode's rule) and 'Andika mwenyewe', then the promise: 'Nimehifadhi ulichoandika.' PARTIAL (work was done without a model): 'Kuandika upya kwa maneno hakupatikani sasa hivi.' + 'Nimefanya nilichoweza bila kufikiri - usafi mdogo.' Offers a gold band ON THE ARTIFACT ITSELF - 'HUU NI USAFI MDOGO WA MAANDISHI - SI AI' - the before/after of the one line changed, 'Weka'/'Acha', and 'Haijaharibu maandishi yako.' SIX RULES IT OBEYS (the deliverable): 1 FIRST PERSON, about herself - 'Sina...', 'Sikuweza...', 'Nitaleta tena nikirudi.'; never her name in the third person from inside her own bubble (app-errors.ts:156 is the model; the shipped 'Sumaiya ana shughuli nyingi' is the bug). 2 NEVER BEG, NEVER BLAME - no 'please try again later', no apology loop, and the wrong reason is ruled out explicitly because this codebase has a documented history of blaming the user's connection for our own faults (app-errors.ts:200-204). 3 NEVER DEAD-END - at least one control that works NOW on every screen; a control may be disabled only with its reason printed beside it (that is the E5 fix). 4 NEVER FAKE SUCCESS - local work is labelled on the OUTPUT, in gold, and only when the output is degraded; nothing is labelled on the good path. 5 THE USER'S WORDS ARE SACRED - kept on screen, never cleared, never re-typed; 'Jaribu tena' resends the same turn so a metered user does not pay twice. 6 THE COMPOSER STAYS OPEN - the user may keep writing while the intelligence is off, the draft line says it is being kept, and the block is on the REPLY, never on the typing (the deliberate opposite of today's editable={!loading}). This replaces the raw English 'AI is not configured.' bubble (routes/ai.ts:157, rendered at QA-WEB-JOURNEYS:63), the third-person busy line, the 'Boresha na AI' that returns the input unchanged (E4), and the disabled save dead-end (E5). VOICE RULE (assumes the app-wide sweep lands on first person; no strings edited here): rail lines are first person ('Ninalinganisha na CV yako', 'Nasoma picha yako'); errors and the unavailable card are first person always; chips name an outcome or are her speaking - 'Tengeneza CV yangu' becomes 'Tengeneza CV yako', and 'Lenga CV kwa kazi' becomes 'Lenga kwenye kazi' (one name, both surfaces); the chat header subtitle 'Msaidizi wako wa kazi' stays because the product is naming her role TO the user; the greeting 'Habari, mimi ni Sumaiya' stays but must be de-duplicated (lead and body say it twice). Surfaces outside the chat flagged for the sibling's sweep, not edited: 'AI ya kazi' (home-screen.tsx:284), 'Msaidizi wa AI' (dashboard/page.tsx:275, cv-editor-client.tsx:3412).

owner_might_reject: R1 The send button becomes a Stop control while she is working - it puts a cancel in the slot every finger goes to and a mistap ends an answer the user paid for; cheap no = cut moves 11 and 10, the rail's footer keeps its own 'Acha' button 40px above the composer, so interruptibility survives without the morph. R2 The composer stays editable while she works (today it is disabled) - risk is one more in-flight turn on metered data; cheap no = keep editable={!loading} and keep only the draft line 'maneno yako yanahifadhiwa' so the user still cannot lose typing, at the cost of C1 staying open. R3 A four-step rail replaces the three dots - 'too much text', and it exposes implementation steps; cheap no = cut to TWO lines (the current step and a quiet 'hatua 2/4' counter), keeping the stop control and elapsed time, and losing the 'it is a plan, not a silence' benefit. R4 A gold 'SI AI' band on any locally-produced result - it looks like an error on a success; cheap no = reduce it to an 11px line in the card footer, or move the disclosure to the 'Jaribu tena' state only - but the disclosure itself must NOT be cut, because 'Boresha na AI' returning the input unchanged is exactly the defect it exists to prevent (E4). R5 'Tengeneza CV yangu' -> 'Tengeneza CV yako' - he may have chosen the first person deliberately; cheap no = one word, one card, fully reversible (rule and measurement in SWAHILI-STANDARD-2026-09-20.md section 4.1). R6 The 200% text-scale gate (2 columns -> 1, no fixed heights) - it can change the look at default size too if done bluntly; cheap no = gate it behind the font scale so the 2x2 grid is unchanged at default, at the cost of ~20% of Android users keeping clipped text. R7 'Futa mazungumzo' behind a confirmation - one more tap on a control he may use often; cheap no = confirm only above N turns, clear instantly below that, at the cost of one irreversible tap on up to 40 turns. R8 Replacing the 1.8s scan ramp with real steps - real steps want server-side events; cheap no = ship the TWO-line version first (upload, then read), which needs no new server work, at the cost of the user still watching a timer they cannot trust. R9 The document card carrying cvId into the editor - it touches the editor's contract, which another agent is editing right now; cheap no = pass initialData plus a sourceCvId and let the editor wire it later, at the cost of M5 (the duplicate CV) staying open. R10 A light version of this chat on WhatsApp - not a design change but a product decision with cost and support implications; cheap no = explicitly out of scope here, raised only because Safaricom's Zuri is the same market and the channel IS the data-cost decision; he can ignore it at zero cost. THE SINGLE RISK HE IS MOST LIKELY TO REJECT OUTRIGHT: R1+R2 together, i.e. 'the composer is never blocked'. It is the one change that alters the SHAPE of the interaction rather than its surface. The presentation that survives a rejection: ship the rail, the receipt, the honest unavailable state and the document card first (all additive and reversible), and put the composer's three states (empty/ready/working) in a second pass behind a flag so he can see it and switch it off.
